entries.title: K class (steam submarine) — recognition diagram
entries.configuration: Surfaced early K-class interpretation with the two retractable steam funnels raised, forward conning tower and two 4-inch deck guns. External lines and equipment stations checked against the 1918 Vickers profile/deck plan. The game fit has eight internal torpedo tubes; removed deck tubes are not added. Simplified plan fittings are original interpretations.

entries.title: Kaichu type — recognition diagram
entries.configuration: Early Kaichu I family proportions and aft-of-tower deck gun, informed by the 1919 Ro-11 photograph. This is an original interpretation of the game’s mixed early Kaichu aggregate, not a claim of an exact Ro-11 fit: the catalog abstracts all six tubes as internal, while individual early boats also carried external trainable tubes. Fine casing and plan detail are reconstructed; no later Kaichu VII conning tower or foredeck gun is substituted.

entries.title: Provana class — recognition diagram
entries.configuration: Original early Barbarigo/Provana recognition diagram using the Italian Navy and ANMI Torino class dimensions and two 76/40 mm deck guns. This represents the 1918 boat, not the 1937 Marcello-class namesake. The museum’s 67 m by 5.90 m dimensions set the proportions; gun stations, casing and fine plan fittings are simplified interpretations. Six internal tubes are not drawn as deck launchers.

entries.title: Bars class submarine — recognition diagram
entries.configuration: Original Bars-family diagram informed by the archival surfaced photograph, with the game’s single 75 mm main gun and two light AA mounts. This is a game-fit interpretation, not a facsimile of a particular dated refit; historical deck armament varied. The catalog represents four internal torpedo tubes, so removed external drop collars are not invented. Hull and small plan detail are simplified.
